NDT inspection software: the four categories of platform

NDT inspection software falls into four broad categories: reporting-only tools, generic ERP and maintenance systems, asset performance and integrity suites, and NDT-native ERP. They solve different problems for different buyers, so the right comparison is category against category first, then product against product within the category that fits you.

Most comparison articles line up a dozen products in one table as if they were interchangeable. They are not. An inspection report app, an accounting-led ERP, a plant integrity suite and an ERP built for NDT contractors have different users, different data models and different ideas of what a job is. Comparing them on the same feature list produces a table full of ticks that tells you nothing.

This comparison is written for North American buyers: owners and managers of NDT and inspection service companies in the USA and Canada, and the QA and operations people who will live with the system. We describe each category honestly, name well-known public products only as examples of a category, and do not make claims about any competitor's pricing or internals. We also say plainly where the Atlantis ERP solution fits and where it does not.

Category 1: reporting-only NDT tools

Reporting-only tools produce inspection reports and little else. This is the category most NDT companies start in, and it includes three kinds of tool.

Spreadsheet and word-processor templates. Excel and Word templates are still the most common NDT reporting system in North America. They are flexible and familiar, and clients often mandate their own spreadsheet formats. The weaknesses are well known: no numbering control, no enforced review, version drift between technicians, retyping from paper, and no link to who was certified or which instrument was calibrated.

Instrument-vendor software. Flaw detector and phased array manufacturers supply PC software to review data and generate reports from their own instruments. These are excellent for analysing that instrument's data. They are not designed to manage reports across every method, crew and client in your company.

Standalone inspection report apps. Mobile form and report apps, some general-purpose and some aimed at inspection, digitise field capture and produce tidy PDFs. They are quick to start with. The question to ask is how method-specific the forms really are, and whether the app knows anything about certifications, calibration, dispatch or billing. Usually it does not, so those stay in spreadsheets.

Reporting-only tools suit a company whose main pain is getting reports out, and who is happy to keep the rest of the business elsewhere.

Category 2: generic ERP, accounting and CMMS platforms

Generic business systems run the finance and operations of companies in every industry. Well-known examples include QuickBooks and NetSuite on the accounting and ERP side, SAP Business One for mid-sized companies, and IBM Maximo as an enterprise asset and maintenance system. Many NDT companies already use one of these, especially for accounting.

Their strength is breadth and maturity: general ledger, payables and receivables, purchasing, payroll integrations, and in the case of maintenance systems, work orders on physical assets. Their weakness, for an NDT service company, is that they do not know what an NDT job is. There is no concept of a PAUT focal law, an RT IQI placement, an SNT-TC-1A Level II in MT, a vision test to Jaeger J1, or a probe that must not leave the shop because its calibration expired yesterday. All of that has to be built as customization or kept in side spreadsheets.

Maintenance systems such as Maximo are usually on the owner-operator side of the fence: the refinery or utility uses it to manage its own equipment and work orders, and the inspection contractor feeds results into it. That makes integration with these systems more important for contractors than replacing them.

Generic platforms suit companies with in-house IT or a budget for a systems integrator, and those whose NDT work is a small part of a larger business.

Category 3: asset performance and integrity management suites

Asset performance management and mechanical integrity suites are built for owner-operators: refineries, petrochemical plants, pipeline operators, power generators and utilities. They organise inspection history around the plant's own equipment hierarchy of units, systems, vessels, piping circuits and tanks, and help integrity engineers plan and document inspection programmes across years.

These suites matter enormously on large Gulf Coast refineries, Alberta oil sands facilities and major US and Canadian utilities. They are typically enterprise purchases, owned by the operator's integrity or reliability group, and configured over long projects. Their users are integrity engineers and plant inspectors rather than contractor dispatchers and field technicians.

For an NDT service company, an integrity suite is usually a destination for data rather than a system you run. Your reports and readings end up in the client's suite. The things that decide whether your own company makes money, such as crew utilisation, technician certifications, instrument calibration, quotes, timesheets and invoices, are simply outside its scope. Buying an integrity suite to run an inspection contractor is like buying a hospital records system to run a staffing agency for nurses.

Integrity suites suit owner-operators with a formal integrity programme and the team to run it. For a contractor, the relevant question is how easily your output can be delivered into your clients' suites.

Category 4: NDT-native ERP

NDT-native ERP is built around the NDT service company itself: its technicians, its certifications, its instruments, its procedures, its jobs, its reports and its invoices. Instead of treating inspection as a generic work order or a generic form, it models the method, the level, the calibration and the code as first-class data.

This is the category the Atlantis ERP solution belongs to. In one system it covers 17 method-specific NDT report types with review and approval; technician certifications by scheme, level and method with automatic expiry status and alerts; vision tests and exam sheets; a revision-controlled procedure register with approval workflow; instruments and probes by serial number with calibration records and a calibration certificate register; team assignments with double-booking blocks and calibration warnings; and quotations, timesheets and invoicing built around NDT jobs, PO numbers, methods and equipment.

The trade-off is focus. An NDT-native ERP is not trying to be a plant integrity suite for an owner-operator, and it will not have the decades of general-industry accounting depth of a large generic ERP. It connects to those systems instead. The Atlantis ERP has an open REST API and can integrate with SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections, scoped per implementation. See the full module list on the ERP apps page.

Which category fits which company

The right inspection management software depends on which side of the job you sit on and how big your team is. As a rule of thumb:

  • Owner-operators with an integrity group (refineries, chemical plants, utilities) belong in category 3 for integrity planning, usually alongside a maintenance system from category 2. They will want contractor data delivered cleanly into those systems.
  • Very small NDT shops doing mostly one or two methods for a few clients can get by with category 1 for a while, provided someone is disciplined about certificates and calibration outside the tool.
  • Diversified companies where NDT is one small division of a large fabricator or engineering firm may reasonably stay on their corporate ERP and add a reporting tool.
  • NDT and inspection service companies, from ten technicians to several hundred, running multiple methods across multiple clients, are the natural fit for category 4, because their profit depends on crews, certifications, instruments and billing working together.

Many contractors end up with a combination: an NDT-native ERP to run the company, their existing accounting package connected through an API, and deliverables sent into clients' integrity systems. That is a sensible architecture. The mistake is trying to force one category to do another category's job.

Where the Atlantis ERP sits, honestly

We would rather you buy the right category than the wrong product, so here is a straight account. The Atlantis ERP solution is built to run an NDT or inspection service company. It is strongest where general tools are weakest: method-specific reporting with offline capture, certification and vision-test tracking with warnings, calibration of instruments by serial number, dispatch that refuses double-bookings and flags out-of-calibration equipment, procedures under revision control, and quoting-to-invoicing that understands NDT jobs.

It is set up and supported by Atlantis NDT, founded by an ASNT NDT Level III, and it is fully customizable: your report templates, your certificate schemes, your invoice layout, and anything that is not a built-in feature configured during implementation. What it is not: it is not a plant integrity suite, it does not hold a client's plant equipment hierarchy, and it does not calculate inspection intervals or corrosion trends. If you are unsure which category you belong in, talk it through with our team.

Using the categories together: integration

Few inspection companies run a single system, and they should not have to. The practical question is how the pieces talk to each other. An NDT contractor typically has three integration points: its accounting system, its clients' maintenance or integrity systems, and its own website and CRM.

On accounting, a common pattern in the US and Canada is to keep QuickBooks or NetSuite as the book of record while the NDT ERP handles jobs, timesheets and invoices, with data passed across through the API. Alternatively, the Atlantis ERP's own invoicing, with job and PO numbers, cost centres and a financial dashboard, can become the primary system. Which way you go is decided during implementation.

On the client side, large owner-operators frequently ask contractors to push results into SAP or Maximo work orders. The Atlantis ERP's open REST API makes that possible, scoped per implementation. On the front end, the website enquiry forms can feed the CRM, where leads carry NDT service type, industry sector, site country and estimated technicians and days, and receive a lead score. Business card scanning turns a trade-show contact into a lead in one step. You can see these modules on the CRM app and Invoicing app pages.

Inspection software for US and Canadian contractors

North American work puts specific demands on inspection software. US contractors report against ASME Section V techniques with acceptance from ASME Section VIII, B31.1 or B31.3, AWS D1.1 on structural steel and API 1104 on pipelines. Canadian contractors add CSA W59, CSA Z662 and provincial authorities such as ABSA in Alberta and TSSA in Ontario. Whatever platform you choose should let every report carry its procedure and standard references; the Atlantis reports capture procedure, standard, WPS, drawing, work order and contract references on each report.

Certification is the other North American wrinkle. US employers typically certify under a written practice to SNT-TC-1A or CP-189, while many Canadian technicians hold NRCan certification to the ISO 9712-based CGSB standard. Contractors working cross-border need a system that holds both side by side. The Atlantis Certificates app records SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP and other schemes with level, method, expiry and vision tests.

Radiography adds regulatory weight on both sides of the border, under the NRC and Agreement States in the US and the CNSC in Canada. The employee profile records radiation safety training, badge number and medical fitness expiry, and the Fleet app records which vehicles can carry sources and their transport licence expiry. Atlantis also offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training through Practical NDT and an eLearning portal.

A short evaluation path

Once you know your category, compare products inside it with a short, disciplined process rather than a long list of demos.

  1. Write a one-page description of how a job moves through your company, from enquiry to paid invoice.
  2. List your methods, your certification schemes, your instrument count and your top three client report formats.
  3. Shortlist two or three products from the category that fits you.
  4. Send each vendor the same job scenario and two of your real report formats before the demo.
  5. In the demo, ask them to finish a report offline, block a double booking, flag an expired certificate and an overdue calibration, and invoice the job with the client PO.
  6. Ask who will implement it, whether they understand NDT, and what your team has to prepare.
  7. Get a scoped quote and plan, then pilot with one crew before rolling out.

If an NDT-native ERP is the right category for you, send us your job scenario and report formats and we will run the demo on them.

Frequently asked questions

What is NDT inspection software?

NDT inspection software is any system that records and manages nondestructive testing work. It ranges from report-only tools, through generic ERP and maintenance systems and plant integrity suites, to NDT-native ERP that runs the whole inspection company around the report.

What is the difference between inspection software and an NDT ERP?

Inspection software often covers only forms and reports. An NDT ERP also manages technician certifications, instrument calibration, crew dispatch, procedures, quotes, timesheets and invoices. The Atlantis ERP solution does all of these in one system.

Is an asset integrity suite a good fit for an NDT contractor?

Usually not as the main system. Integrity suites are built for owner-operators to organise inspection history around their own plant equipment. Contractors typically deliver data into them while running their own business on an NDT-native ERP.

Can the Atlantis ERP work with SAP, Maximo or QuickBooks?

Yes. The Atlantis ERP has an open REST API and can integrate with SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections. The scope is agreed per implementation.

Which NDT methods does the Atlantis ERP report on?

It has 17 report types: UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS, PAUT, MFL, TOFD, PWHT, PMI, hardness, UT thickness, ferrite, holiday/coating and computed radiography, each with its own numbering sequence.

How is the Atlantis ERP priced?

Each setup is scoped to your methods, team size and integrations, so pricing is quote on request. It is positioned as affordable, accessible and fully customizable for small and mid-sized NDT companies.
